paradoxes.text: Indispensability is the exposure. The more Singapore lodges both great powers in its economy and its bases - US access at Changi and the F-35s, China as first trading partner and a rising source of investment - the more each can demand and the more it loses when they collide. Wong foresees US-China trade grinding to a halt and warns of a miscalculation over Taiwan; Balakrishnan calls Hormuz a possible dry run for the Pacific. The small state that cannot choose is the first to be squeezed when choosing is forced.

paradoxes.text: Solving the land problem abroad creates levers at home. The SAF trains in Taiwan (since 1975), Australia and the United States because the island is too small; when Hong Kong customs seized nine Terrex vehicles returning from Taiwan in November 2016, Beijing used the training as a diplomatic weapon and the vehicles were returned only in January 2017. The more of the force lives overseas, the more its hosts - and the hosts' enemies - hold a hostage.

paradoxes.text: The rule that protects the small state binds its own hand. grand_strategy.reading:
Singapore is Luttwak's small state that cannot win a contest of weight and so plays
the other game: it makes itself indispensable to everyone. It lodges the American navy
at Changi, buys American F-35s, trades more with China than with anyone, signs a
partnership with every capital that matters and keeps a budget near 3% of GDP for a
force that trains on other people's land. The logic is sound while the great powers
compete at a distance; it inverts when they collide, because the state that served
both is the first place where each can be denied to the other (the chip diversion
cases and the cyber intrusion are early tremors). Wong's doctrine for a disordered
world is to say so openly - rules for all, no forced choice, 'useful but not used' -
and to spend the political capital of a 65.57% mandate on shock absorbers: stored
wealth, replacement LNG, a 2061 water horizon and a Johor zone that turns the
neighbour from a lever into a stakeholder. What the strategy cannot fix is the
arithmetic underneath: a fertility rate of 0.87 and a labour force that must keep
arriving from abroad.

stances.note: Close to an ally without a treaty. The 1990 MoU gives US forces access to Singapore's military facilities (Changi Naval Base added by a 1998 addendum), the 2005 Strategic Framework Agreement made Singapore a 'Major Security Cooperation Partner', and the 2019 protocol renewed the MoU for 15 years (to about 2035). Singapore is buying 20 F-35s. Frictions are economic: a 10% baseline tariff since April 2025 (15% announced in February 2026, not yet directed on 5 March; current status not verified), US pressure on AI-chip diversion, and no confirmed Wong-Trump bilateral in 2025 (they shared the ASEAN family photo in Kuala Lumpur on 26 Oct 2025); Wong and Trump spoke by telephone on 2 Jan 2026 for the 60th anniversary of ties and Singapore was invited to the December 2026 G20 in Miami. Wong: 'America is a Pacific power.' Bond - none: pure interest, our reading.

stances.note: The relationship was upgraded in 2023 to an 'all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership'; Xi received Wong in Beijing in June 2025, Li Qiang visited Singapore on 25 Oct 2025, and both sides marked 35 years of ties in October 2025.
